column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3e timing of cash flows and 3a, the case dates the ten and ties them to no building (quote exact, case l.88-89); fix the claim that the contribution has no date: the case calls it her 2033 contribution (l.110, l.117-118), decided after the reserve (l.101), so say it has a year but no day; Table 3 stays at seven rows.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, what the 2031 range is a statement of: the case's own verb is expects to contribute (l.110), a figure stated in 2031 and paid in 2033; consistent with SKELETON 3d, where the bottom is stated in writing but nothing moves before 2033.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b, ownership not a clause keeps a cancelled building from costing her anything she owns (IPS l.15); fix wording: both ends sit in Treasuries only from the 2031 move to December 2032 (the top is in VT before), say the funds pay about $123,476 at today's market rates, and never show that figure in 3d (Q25); held for her, never in her name (Q72, UCC 8-503); Niche overstated, a Keel reading.

Mon 16 Nov: the case says Laura will make ten payments (l.88) and the IPS calls the commitment fixed and non-negotiable; a scenario where the ten lapse and the $444,545 reserve returns to her is an exit in all but name beside IPS l.17's two reasons; keep only row 5's fact that nothing held depends on the building.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e one clause, a late building forces no sale: IBTM and the moved half end in cash and wait in the Treasury-bill ETF (NUMBERS 0, TNA l.5); SKELETON 3d already carries the funder's note that the contribution waits until the first draw, so this is its store home; which T-bill ETF stays UNVERIFIED (NUMBERS 7).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e, not a NUMBERS figure: $3,450 a year is Keel arithmetic on 8d's 3.0%; label it so, net it against what the waiting money earns in the Treasury-bill ETF and the Taiwan dollar, and file it under the IPS's first use (building costs that overrun), never one more use beside the three IPS l.15 names.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; Cardozo held the duty to perpetuate the name sufficient (quote checked), but the promissory estoppel words come from a sentence saying it is needless to consider whether one may result, so it is not a holding: drop or say left open.

Mon 16 Nov: store only, the will condition is quoted exactly (checked at source); a neat parallel for the case's own order (reserve first, l.94 and l.101), but the case already sets that order, so no part needs it.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; quotes check, but he endorsed notes (a guaranty) and estoppel bound him once building began; the use (name the facility as a condition in her 2031 words) must first be squared with SKELETON 3d, where her figure is first and unconditional.

Mon 16 Nov: the barrier plus right of return or release test is Q18-001 and H3-109; the new use (payable when construction begins) clashes with SKELETON 3d's first and unconditional figure and would make her figure hang on others' money.
Mon 16 Nov: art. 408 is Q55-035; the part-transfer clause is quoted exactly (MOJ English, checked) but adds nothing a part needs (case l.169).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; rests on 1904 trial findings recorded on appeal with the appellate result unread, so it cannot carry a by default claim until the outcome is read.

Mon 16 Nov: store only, UPMIFA s.6(a) quoted exactly (Va. Code 64.2-1104(A) checked): consent redirects within charity, never home; adds to Q7c-011 the bar on non-charitable use; institutional fund coverage varies by state.
Mon 16 Nov: s.6(c) text checked at Va. Code; the court route with notice to the Attorney General is already Q7c-011, and H4-052 already rejects cy-pres for the report.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, UTC s.413(b) checked at the New Hampshire page; applies to charitable trusts, not outright gifts, so the use should say a trust.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the quoted sentence is the court's statement of the common-law rule (the holding is that CUMIFA did not change it), so say stated, not held; off every part.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, quote checked in the guidebook (p.10): return, written consent or a court; it also contradicts row 40's usually stays in charity, which matters for that row.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, New York's consent-or-cy-pres route for restricted campaign money; COVID-era guidance, passages read.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, a shrunk or moved project as a changed purpose (Mississippi AG 2024); with row 17 it shows US return is common, not rare.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, never in the report: a naming dispute, off the case; the CPI repayment detail is its only link.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; s.63 paraphrase checked as enacted, but the Charities Act 2022 changed failed-appeal rules (unread), and opposite of America's overclaims given rows 17, 19 and 31: say as enacted in 2011 and drop the contrast.
Mon 16 Nov: store only (case l.169); arts. 412 and 419 quoted exactly from the MOJ English; 412 applies once the gift is delivered and the donee fails the charge.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; art. 33 para. 1 and 3 checked in the Chinese text (para. 3 has two exceptions sending even that to the local government); SKELETON 3d cuts the Foundations Act as outside the case (l.169).

Mon 16 Nov: store only; art. 14(1) is misquoted: the ban covers transfers to the founder made by collusion, fraud or other improper means (以通謀、詐欺或其他不正當手段), not every transfer, so no back door overclaims; art. 22(1) checks.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, Massachusetts' repay-immediately rule for cultural facility grants; Taiwan's own grant clawbacks are Q48.

Mon 16 Nov: store only, the contract let before land and funding and the Commission's lesson are new to the store (Q67 holds pledges and maintenance); restates aha 4 if used, so 3d at most a clause.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store, a 2025 cultural building ended for construction costs with donors offered reclaim or reaffirm; the IPS's first use in life; page not reachable on re-check, passages only.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d; payable when built makes her the last money and a start-by lapse makes her figure conditional, both against SKELETON 3d (her figure first and unconditional, Kresge-style co-sponsors last); keep at most purpose named (the facility) and nothing paid before 2033; Keel synthesis, never in Laura's words as law.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b; usually stays in charity is contradicted by the card's own rows 17, 19 and 31, and the protection lasts only until she pays in 2033; legal comparisons are outside the case (l.169); keep the plain point, that until 2033 a cancelled building costs her nothing she owns, without restating aha 4.
Mon 16 Nov: Cloud Gate's seven years from fire to opening and its slipped timetable are already Q11d-029.
